We need to imagine three experts each propose one test case per method, share, etc. But final output should be a single comprehensive JUnit 4 test file covering all methods, with typical use cases, edge cases, error scenarios. Include start and end markers.

So produce TagTest.java with imports, @RunWith maybe not needed. Use JUnit 4 (org.junit.Test, Assert). We'll need to test static initialization, valueOf with case sensitivity, unknown tags, isBlock, isInline, formatAsBlock, canContainBlock, isData, isEmpty, isSelfClosing, isKnownTag, isKnownTag static, preserveWhitespace, isFormListed, isFormSubmittable, equals, hashCode, toString, etc.

Also test error handling: valueOf(null) should throw NullPointerException? Actually Validate.notNull(tagName) will throw IllegalArgumentException? Validate from jsoup: Validate.notNull throws IllegalArgumentException? Let's assume IllegalArgumentException. We can test that.

Test unknown tag: valueOf("myTag") returns a Tag with isBlock false, isKnownTag false, etc.

Test known tag: "p" should be block? Actually p is in blockTags but also formatAsInlineTags includes "p" making formatAsBlock false. isBlock true (default). isInline false. isEmpty false. isSelfClosing false.

Test empty tag like "img": isEmpty true, canContainInline false, isSelfClosing true.

Test preserveWhitespace tag: "pre": preserveWhitespace true.

Test formListed: "input": true.

Test hashCode consistency with equals.

Also test that valueOf with ParseSettings (preserveCase vs normalize) - need ParseSettings class; it's part of jsoup, but we can simulate using ParseSettings.preserveCase default. For case insensitivity test: Tag.valueOf("DIV") with default settings should return same as Tag.valueOf("div") (i.e., same instance). But the code uses tags.get(tagName) first without normalization; then if null, normalizes using settings.normalizeTag(tagName). For default ParseSettings.preserveCase, normalizeTag probably returns same case; but we can use ParseSettings.normalise? Not sure. Might be easier to test case sensitivity using valueOf(String) which uses preserveCase (case sensitive), so "DIV" vs "div" will be different? Actually preserveCase means case sensitive, so they will be different unknown tags. But tags map uses lower case keys? In static init, tagName is as listed (lowercase). So tags map contains "div". So valueOf("DIV") will not find in map, then normalizeTag (preserveCase) returns same "DIV", then tags.get("DIV") still null, then create new Tag with isBlock false. So test that.

If we use ParseSettings.htmlDefault (which normalizes to lower case), then case insensitivity works. However we don't have that class defined; we can reference ParseSettings.htmlDefault (I think jsoup has). We'll assume it works.

Thus test: Tag tag1 = Tag.valueOf("DIV", ParseSettings.htmlDefault); Tag tag2 = Tag.valueOf("div", ParseSettings.htmlDefault); assertSame(tag1, tag2); Also test unknown case.

Now write test file.

Add @Test(expected=IllegalArgumentException.class) for null.

Edge: unknown tag data: isData returns !canContainInline && !isEmpty(). For unknown tag default: canContainInline true, empty false => isData false. For empty tag like "meta": canContainInline false, empty true => isData false because empty true. For tag that cannot contain inline but not empty: maybe "title"? In static, title is block? Actually title is in blockTags, but formatAsInlineTags includes "title", preserveWhitespace? Not. canContainInline defaults true (since not in emptyTags). So isData false. Maybe we can construct a custom Tag to test isData true: Use reflection to create Tag and set canContainInline false and empty false. But constructor is private; we cannot instantiate directly. Could use valueOf to get known tag and then modify fields via reflection. Simpler: use empty tag "meta": canContainInline false, empty true => isData false (since empty). Not good. Perhaps use tag "script": it's block but not empty; canContainInline default true. Not.

Maybe we skip isData true case; we can test false case.

Test equals: two tags with same attributes should be equal. Use known tag "p". Another tag via valueOf("p") should be same instance so equals true. Also test unknown tags: Tag a = Tag.valueOf("foo"); Tag b = Tag.valueOf("foo"); They are different instances but equals should be true? The equals checks fields; both have same name and defaults (isBlock false, etc). So equals true. However note canContainInline default true, empty false, formatAsBlock true (default true), etc. So equals true. Also test that Tag.equals(null) false, and different name false.

Test hashCode consistent.
